case_name: Ram Chandra Shukla v State of Uttar Pradesh and others
facts: The appellant was a member of the Higher Judicial Service in the State of Uttar Pradesh.
He was posted as Additional District and Sessions Judge at Etah, Uttar Pradesh.
By order dated 17-4-1997, his services were terminated, preceded by an inquiry conducted by a learned Judge of the Allahabad High Court.
The inquiry report submitted by the learned Judge was considered in a Full Court Meeting of the Allahabad High Court and the report was accepted.
Pursuant thereto, his services were terminated.
He filed a writ petition before the High Court, which was dismissed after threadbare discussion of the law.
Hence, this appeal by special leave.
petitioner_arguments: Considering the fact that the offence committed by the appellant is only a fraction and not actuated with malice or dishonesty, the punishment of dismissal imposed on him is disproportionate with the offence charged and proved against him.
court_reasoning: It is a serious judicial misconduct on the part of the appellant which would attract the penalty of dismissal from service.
We are unable to countenance this submission of the learned counsel for the appellant.

As a member of the Higher Judicial Service, it was not expected of the appellant to have granted bail to the accused which had earlier been rejected by the District Judge, in charge of the District and by the High Court.
holding: The appellant shall be paid the amount due to him within a period of two months from the date of receipt of this order
cases_cited: Ram Chandra Shukla v State of Uttar Pradesh
